content: Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of nilotinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Additionally, phenobarbital decreases nilotinib levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Nitrous oxide and phenobarbital both enhance sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while norepinephrine reduces it. The interaction effect is unclear; caution is advised. Phenobarbital and nortriptyline both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids and nortriptyline both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Caution and monitoring are required. Belladonna alkaloids reduce olanzapine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Phenobarbital and olanzapine both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids also reduce olanzapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral forms. Olanzapine enhances the effects of belladonna alkaloids via pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital decreases olanzapine levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital and olanzapine/samidorphan may mutually enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of diazepam, alcohol, or other CNS-acting drugs with olanzapine may potentiate orthostatic hypotension and additive sedation. Caution and monitoring are required. Belladonna alkaloids increase the toxicity of oliceridine through mechanisms involving anticholinergic effects, which may elevate the risk of urinary retention and/or severe constipation, potentially leading to paralytic ileus. Monitoring for signs of urinary retention or reduced gastric motility is essential when oliceridine is co-administered with anticholinergics. Phenobarbital reduces oliceridine levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. If co-administration with a CYP3A4 inducer is necessary, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable drug effects are achieved, while monitoring for signs of opioid withdrawal. If the inducer is discontinued, reduce the oliceridine dosage and monitor for respiratory depression. Phenobarbital decreases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital reduces ondansetron levels or effects by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. No dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended for patients on these drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital and opium tincture both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Oritavancin increases phenobarbital levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Oritavancin is a weak CYP2C9 inhibitor; caution is advised when co-administered with CYP2C9 substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. Orlistat reduces phenobarbital levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral forms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required due to the risk of convulsions. Belladonna alkaloids and orphenadrine both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Phenobarbital and orphenadrine both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital decreases osilodrostat levels or effects through mechanisms involving CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust the osilodrostat dose as needed during co-administration with strong CYP3A4 and/or CYP2B6 inducers, and monitor for signs and symptoms during administration and discontinuation. Belladonna alkaloids and oxybutynin both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital decreases ospemifene levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Phenobarbital and oxazepam both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Belladonna alkaloids and oxybutynin (topical or transdermal) both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital and oxycodone both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces oxycodone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital and oxymorphone both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital decreases paclitaxel levels or effects through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity and other mechanisms, including CYP2C8 induction. Caution and monitoring are required. Belladonna alkaloids reduce paliperidone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Phenobarbital decreases paliperidone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Phenobarbital and paliperidone both increase sedation. Paliperidone enhances the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital decreases pazopanib levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital reduces penbutolol levels by increasing metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration of phenobarbital. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital and pentazocine both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces polatuzumab vedotin levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer may decrease unconjugated MMAE AUC. Caution and monitoring are necessary.
